themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded to 19 THIS WEEK, a 744% spike compared to the 2.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.33), suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors or enforcement crackdown on the Upper East Side.
evidence: 19 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 average over prior 8 weeks (744% increase)
Z-score of 11.33 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Complaints concentrate in a single week, suggesting acute event rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed food vendors proliferating in specific neighborhoods (near parks, transit hubs)? Interview DOHMH, vendor associations, and residents.
Is the city conducting a targeted enforcement operation? Check with Department of Consumer Affairs for vendor citations or compliance sweeps.

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals & Urban Decay
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 9 THIS WEEK, a 243% increase from the 2.6-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.23), and dead/dying tree complaints reached 4 complaints 2 weeks ago (967% spike from 0.4 avg), suggesting potential public health and environmental maintenance failures.
evidence: 9 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average (243% spike, z-score: 5.23)
4 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score: 5.21)
Two concurrent spikes in environmental decay indicators suggest systemic sanitation or Parks maintenance failure
reporting_angles: Is Parks Department staffing adequate for animal removal and tree maintenance? Interview Parks officials about response times.
Are specific parks or blocks being neglected? Map complaints geographically to identify hotspots and document conditions.

themes_detail.label: Commercial Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Commercial disposal complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK, an 860% spike compared to the 0.6-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 7.72), indicating potential widespread business sanitation or dumpster management failures across the district.
evidence: 6 commercial disposal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% increase, z-score: 7.72)
Dumpster complaints also spiked to 3 LAST WEEK (700% increase from 0.4 avg, z-score: 5.42)
Paired spikes suggest concentrated commercial waste management problem
reporting_angles: Which businesses or commercial zones are violating disposal rules? Cross-reference complaints with DOE violations and interview Sanitation Department.
Is this tied to construction activity? The district filed 1,956 building permits in 90 days (1,767 alterations); assess whether renovation-driven waste is overwhelming disposal capacity.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Accelerates
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints reached 229 LAST WEEK, a 75% increase from the 130.6-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.38), extending an already high-volume complaint category into crisis territory amid heavy construction activity.
evidence: 229 illegal parking complaints LAST WEEK vs. 130.6 weekly average (75% spike, z-score: 6.38)
Illegal parking is the top complaint category overall (1,842 in 90 days) with acute weekly surge
Coincides with 1,956 building permits filed in 90 days (47 new buildings, 14 full demolitions), suggesting construction vehicles and worker parking pressure
reporting_angles: Are construction sites generating illegal parking? Interview DOT and HPD about permit conditions and enforcement near major projects like 655 Madison Avenue.
Which streets are worst hit? Map complaints to identify neighborhoods and interview residents about impact on street access and safety.

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints doubled to 24 LAST WEEK, a 126% increase from the 10.6-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.15), signaling growing problems with Uber, Lyft, or other app-based services on the Upper East Side.
evidence: 24 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 10.6 weekly average (126% increase, z-score: 5.15)
Spike aligns with illegal parking surge, suggesting vehicles congregating or idling in violation of traffic rules
Unpredictable surge suggests either driver behavior change or enforcement shift
reporting_angles: Are for-hire drivers causing traffic, blocking bus lanes, or creating safety hazards? Observe hotspots and interview residents and transit advocates.
Has TLC enforcement changed, or are ride-hailing services expanding service in the district? Interview TLC officials about complaint patterns and driver compliance.
